scope: Close a bounded 7AG.4 gap by rejecting known Visual Studio/MSVC developer-environment selectors until a content-bound Windows toolchain profile exists.

method.kind: Primary Microsoft build-environment documentation plus controlled-builder self-tests

findings.documentedEffect: Microsoft documents PATH, TMP, INCLUDE, LIB, LIBPATH, and additional tool/platform/SDK-specific environment variables as inputs to command-line builds.
findings.sourceLimit: The documentation does not imply that every variable changes every build. It establishes that environment selection can affect tool and SDK resolution.
findings.builderDisposition: Known Visual Studio/MSVC selectors are rejected when non-empty in controlled builds until a Windows content-closure profile exists.

findings.documentedEffect: Microsoft's C++ configuration guidance uses WindowsSdkDir and VCToolsInstallDir in SDK/toolset include paths and notes that they may be defined by a developer command prompt rather than being global environment variables.
findings.builderDisposition: If these and related roots are present in the inherited environment, the controlled build fails closed; no value is serialized.

findings.documentedEffect: Microsoft documents VSCMD_VER as set by the Developer Command Prompt and recommends it to detect that environment.
findings.builderDisposition: All non-empty VSCMD_* variables are conservatively rejected, including unrecognized future suffixes.

implementation.controlledEnvironmentPolicy: Reject named Visual Studio/MSVC install, toolset, SDK and runtime roots, plus all non-empty VSCMD_* environment keys; error output names variables only.

nextGate: Keep native MSVC unavailable for qualification until the selected compiler/toolset/SDK inputs, effective link inputs, and runtime dependencies are content-bound and checked. Continue unrelated local implementation slices without waiting for Windows availability.
